subject: general
question: The growth rate of the Christian population in India between 2001 and 2011 was ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**15.5%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census 2011** data, the decadal growth rate of the **Christian population** in India between **2001 and 2011** was recorded as **15.5%**.
 
• In absolute terms, the **Christian population** increased from **2.41 crore** in the **2001 Census** to **2.78 crore** in the **2011 Census**.
 
• Despite the numerical increase, the **percentage share** of Christians in the total population of India remained stable at **2.3%** across the decade.
 
• This growth rate of **15.5%** was lower than the **national average growth rate** of **17.7%** recorded for the same period (**2001-2011**).
 
• The religious data of the **2011 Census** was officially released by the **Registrar General and Census Commissioner** of India in **August 2015**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Growth Rates of Other Religions (2001-2011):**

 
 
• **Hindus**: The growth rate of the Hindu population was **16.8%**, with their total population reaching **96.63 crore**.
 
• **Muslims**: This community registered the highest growth rate among the major religious groups at **24.6%**, reaching a total of **17.22 crore**.
 
• **Sikhs**: The growth rate for the Sikh population was recorded at **8.4%**, totaling **2.08 crore**.
 
• **Buddhists and Jains**: The growth rates were **6.1%** and **5.4%** respectively, reflecting a slower growth compared to other major groups.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Distribution of Christians:**
 
 
• In terms of **geographical distribution**, the highest concentration of Christians is found in the **Southern and Northeastern states** of India.
 
• The state of **Kerala** has the largest **absolute number** of Christians in the country.
 
• States like **Nagaland, Mizoram, and Meghalaya** are Christian-majority states, where they constitute over **70-80%** of the local population.
 
• **Goa** also maintains a significant Christian population, contributing to the cultural and demographic diversity of the **Western Coast**.
 
 
 
• **Census Administration:**
 
 
• The **Census** in India is conducted under the **Census Act, 1948**, and is a decennial exercise.
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs** is the nodal ministry responsible for conducting the census through the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **2011 Census** was the **15th National Census** of India since **1872** and the **7th** after **Independence**.
 
• The total population of India in **2011** was **121.09 crore**, which represented an increase of **18.15 crore** from the **2001** figures.
 
• The data on **Religious Communities** is vital for understanding the **socio-economic** changes and for the effective implementation of **government welfare schemes** targeted at **minority communities**.
